proposals.title: Requirements
proposals.statement: 2.11 Product Quality Requirements 22

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: It describes the required structure, evidence and review expectations for the architecture of an individual product.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: A product architecture must be useful for engineering.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: It should help teams build, test, integrate, secure, deploy, release, maintain and evolve the product.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: It should not be written only for review.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: It must be accurate enough to support implementation and stable enough to support future change.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: The goal of this document is therefore to define the minimum product architecture evidence required to make a product implementable, testable, securable, deployable, releasable, maintainable and compatible with applicable solution baselines and enterprise guardrails.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: A product architecture should answer four practical questions:

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: A product architecture shall be updated when significant design decisions change, when interfaces change, when deployment assumptions change, when security assumptions change, or when product technical debt affects solution compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: It must be detailed enough that developers can build the product, testers can verify it, security roles can assess it, integrators can connect it, and release owners can decide whether it is ready.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Level Architecture / Product Level Architecture Scope
proposals.statement: The Product Architect is responsible for showing how the product is structured, how it behaves, how it is deployed, how it exposes or consumes interfaces, and how it satisfies quality, security and verification expectations.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Level Architecture / Product Level Architecture Scope
proposals.statement: When a product participates in a solution, Product Architecture must provide the evidence needed by Solution Architecture to assess integration readiness and release compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Level Architecture / Product Level Architecture Scope
proposals.statement: Quality attributes | Define measurable non-functional requirements

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture
proposals.statement: The product should not only describe its internal components.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture
proposals.statement: It should also explain why the product exists, which solution capability it supports, which enterprise and solution guardrails apply, which processes are required to verify it, and who owns the critical architecture elements.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Backlog refinement, CI/CD, architecture review, testing, security verification, release readiness, debt management

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | Product architect, product owner, development team, test owner, security owner, interface owner

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture
proposals.statement: Instead, it identifies the product-level architecture areas where BAPO alignment must be made explicit.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture
proposals.statement: For each area, the Product Architect must ensure that the business relevance is understood, the architecture responsibility is defined, the required delivery and verification mechanisms exist, and ownership is clear.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture / Product Level Architecture Deliverables Overview
proposals.statement: At product level, architecture deliverables form the minimum evidence package required to understand, govern, integrate, verify and release an individual product.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture / Product Level Architecture Deliverables Overview
proposals.statement: These deliverables show how the product contributes to business or mission value, how it is architected internally, how it exposes or consumes interfaces, how quality and security requirements are addressed, and how compatibility with solution baselines and enterprise guardrails is demonstrated.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture / Product Level Architecture Deliverables Overview
proposals.statement: What matters is that each deliverable is owned, versioned, reviewable and supported by evidence where required.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture / Product Level Architecture Deliverables Overview
proposals.statement: Quality Requirement Catalogue | Measurable product quality attributes

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Product Architecture / Product Level Architecture Deliverables Overview
proposals.statement: Product Process Evidence | Shows CI/CD, test, security, release, and debt-management mechanisms required by the architecture

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / The Product Business Contribution Statement
proposals.statement: It should be short, specific and architecture-relevant.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / The Product Business Contribution Statement
proposals.statement: It should not become a marketing description.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / The Product Business Contribution Statement
proposals.statement: The statement should clarify the product's contribution in terms that are useful for architecture decisions.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / The Product Business Contribution Statement
proposals.statement: It should explain which capability the product enables, which solution context it supports, which users or systems depend on it, and which architecture qualities are critical for that contribution.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / The Product Business Contribution Statement
proposals.statement: A good Product Business Contribution Statement should answer the following questions:

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Context and Scope
proposals.statement: It should define what the product owns and what it does not own.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Context and Scope
proposals.statement: It should also identify all external systems and actors that influence product behavior.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Context and Scope
proposals.statement: They prevent false expectations and help Solution Architects understand where additional products, platforms, or services are required.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: It shall show more than components, modules or services.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: It must also explain what each building block is responsible for, which interfaces it provides or consumes, which dependencies it has, which quality attributes it supports, and who owns it.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: Each building block should have a clear purpose, clear boundaries, clear interfaces, clear ownership and a clear relationship to the product's quality requirements.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: The Building Block View should also show where architecture-relevant quality attributes are implemented.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: For example, if a product claims resilience, the architecture should show which building blocks implement retry, buffering, failover, monitoring, recovery or degraded-mode behavior.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: If a product claims security, the architecture should show where authentication, authorization, crypto, logging or audit responsibilities are implemented.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: Required element | Purpose | Required content / evidence

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: Quality attribute allocation | Shows where important quality requirements are implemented in the architecture. | Resilience mechanisms, performance-critical components, security controls, observability points, recovery logic

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: The Building Block View should focus on architecture-relevant building blocks, not on every implementation detail.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: The Building Block View should be consistent with the Runtime View, Deployment View, Interface Specification, ADR Register and Quality Requirement Catalogue.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: If a building block exposes an interface, this interface should also appear in the interface specification.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: If a building block implements an important runtime behavior, this should be reflected in the runtime view.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: If a building block exists because of a major architecture decision, the rationale should be traceable to an ADR.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: Where responsibilities, ownership, dependencies or quality allocations are unclear, the gap should be captured as product architecture debt.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Building Block View
proposals.statement: A product architecture should not be considered complete if the building blocks are visible as boxes but their responsibilities, interfaces, dependencies and ownership remain ambiguous.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: The runtime view is required because many architecture risks only become visible during execution.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: Runtime scenarios | Define the most important execution situations the product must support. | Main operational scenarios, failure scenarios, degraded scenarios, DIL scenarios, startup and shutdown scenarios

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: The runtime view should be based on the scenarios that matter most for the product's business contribution, solution participation and quality requirements.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: It should not attempt to describe every possible execution path.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: Instead, it should focus on the runtime behavior that is architecture-relevant, risk-relevant or required for integration, verification and release readiness.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: Each runtime scenario should identify the involved building blocks, external systems, interfaces, data exchanges, state changes, timing assumptions, error conditions and expected evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: Where the product participates in a solution, the runtime view must also show the externally visible behavior needed by Solution Architecture to assess integration readiness and release compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: The runtime view should be maintained together with the building block view, deployment view, interface specifications, quality requirements, security concept and verification evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Runtime View
proposals.statement: If runtime behavior changes, the affected ADRs, tests, interface contracts, deployment assumptions and release compatibility declarations should be reviewed as well.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: The Deployment View is required because deployment assumptions directly affect product quality, release readiness and solution compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: Runtime assumptions | Defines the technical environment required to execute the product. | Operating system, container runtime, orchestration, network assumptions, storage assumptions, middleware, platform services

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: The Deployment View should focus on deployment aspects that are architecture-relevant, release-relevant or risk-relevant.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: It does not need to describe every operational detail, but it must provide enough information to understand whether the product can be deployed, configured, observed, updated and recovered in the environments for which it is intended.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: The Deployment View should be consistent with the Runtime View, Interface Specification, Product Security Concept, Quality Requirement Catalogue and Product Release Compatibility Declaration.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: If the product depends on a specific runtime, network condition, platform service, container configuration, storage model or security control, this dependency should be visible in the Deployment View and verified through suitable evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: Where a product participates in a solution, the Deployment View must also support Solution Architecture.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: It should show whether the product's deployment assumptions are compatible with the solution deployment topology, runtime environment, observability model, security boundaries and release baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: If deployment assumptions differ between product and solution level, the gap should be captured as product technical debt, solution deployment risk or architecture runway.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: A product should not be considered deployment-ready if deployment is manual, undocumented, environment-specific, untested or not reproducible.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Deployment View
proposals.statement: Missing deployment automation, unclear configuration, insufficient observability, missing rollback strategy or unverified environment compatibility should be treated as release-readiness risks.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: A product should not release an interface or data contract change without understanding the solution-level impact.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: Each interface and data contract shall therefore be treated as a managed architecture artifact.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: It must have a clear purpose, owner, version, compatibility rule, schema, semantics, security assumptions, error-handling behavior and verification evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: Security | Defines how the interface or data exchange is protected. | Authentication, authorization, crypto, classification, trust zone, audit requirement, logging requirement

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: The specification should be detailed enough for another product team to implement, consume, test and verify the interface without relying on informal knowledge.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: It should describe not only the technical structure of the interface, but also its meaning, ownership, compatibility expectations, security assumptions and operational behavior.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: Interface and data contract changes must be assessed against the relevant solution baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: A change may be acceptable at product level but still create solution-level incompatibility if consumers are not ready, schemas are no longer compatible, semantic meaning changes, security assumptions differ, or required contract tests are missing.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: Such changes should be reviewed with the Solution Architect before release.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: Where interfaces or data contracts are incomplete, unowned, unversioned, untested or semantically unclear, the gap should be captured as product architecture debt or solution integration risk.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Interface and Data Contract Specification
proposals.statement: A product should not be considered release-ready if externally visible interfaces or data contracts required by the solution baseline are not specified, versioned, owned and verified.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: They explain not only what was built, but why it was built that way, which alternatives were considered, which trade-offs were accepted, and which consequences must be managed over time.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: ADRs are required because future teams, reviewers and solution architects need to understand the rationale behind major product decisions.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: This creates risk when products evolve, teams change, interfaces are reused, solution baselines change, or technical debt needs to be assessed.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: Each relevant ADR should connect the business driver, architecture decision, process implication, ownership implication, affected quality markers and verification evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: ADR field | Purpose | Required content

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: Process implication | Defines what must happen in delivery, verification or governance because of the decision. | Required tests, reviews, release rules, pipeline changes, governance steps, documentation updates

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: Review date | Defines when the decision should be reassessed. | Review date, trigger condition, expiry condition, supersession link if applicable

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: ADRs should be created for decisions that materially affect product structure, interfaces, data contracts, runtime behavior, deployment assumptions, security controls, quality attributes, technology choices, solution compatibility or alignment with enterprise guardrails.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: Not every implementation detail requires an ADR.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: The ADR discipline should focus on decisions that would be difficult, risky or costly to reverse, or decisions that future teams would not be able to understand from the implementation alone.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: The test is simple: if a future reviewer would ask “why was this done this way?”, an ADR is likely required.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: ADRs should remain linked to the Product Architecture Document, Interface Specification, Data Contract Specification, Quality Requirement Catalogue, Product Security Concept, Verification Evidence and Product Release Compatibility Declaration.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: If an ADR affects a solution-level interface, data flow, deployment model or security boundary, it should also be visible to the Solution Architect.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: An ADR should not be treated as final forever.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Architecture Decision Records
proposals.statement: Deprecated or superseded ADRs should remain available so that the architecture history remains traceable.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Product quality requirements define the measurable non-functional expectations that the product architecture must satisfy.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: They translate architecture claims such as performance, resilience, security, interoperability or deployability into concrete requirements that can be designed, implemented, verified and reviewed.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Quality requirements must not remain generic statements.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: A product should not only claim to be “secure”, “performant” or “resilient”.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: The architecture must define what this means for the product, where the requirement is implemented, which evidence proves it, and who owns the requirement.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Product quality requirements therefore connect architecture design to verification evidence, release readiness and technical debt management.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: The following quality attributes define the minimum product-level quality requirement set:

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Quality attribute | Purpose | Required content / evidence

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Determinism | Ensures predictable timing and behavior where required by mission or system constraints. | Scheduling rules, prioritization, timing assumptions, deterministic execution constraints, timing analysis, test results

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Performance | Ensures that the product meets required latency, throughput and resource expectations. | Latency budgets, throughput targets, resource budgets, load tests, performance measurements

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Each quality requirement should be measurable or otherwise reviewable.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Where a numeric threshold is meaningful, it should be stated explicitly, for example latency, throughput, recovery time, resource usage or availability target.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Where a numeric threshold is not sufficient, the requirement should define observable behavior, acceptance criteria, test approach or review evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Product quality requirements should be linked to the relevant architecture views.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Performance and determinism should be reflected in the Runtime View.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Deployability should be reflected in the Deployment View.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Interoperability should be reflected in the Interface and Data Contract Specification.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Security requirements should be reflected in the Product Security Concept.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Maintainability and major trade-offs should be traceable to ADRs.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Quality requirements should also be linked to verification evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: A product should not be considered release-ready if important quality attributes are only described but not verified.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Missing or weak evidence should be captured as product technical debt, architecture runway, verification backlog or release-readiness risk.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: The Product Architect is responsible for ensuring that quality requirements are architecturally defined and traceable.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Product teams are responsible for implementation and evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Quality Requirements
proposals.statement: Security, Platform, Data and Solution Architects should be involved where the quality requirement affects cross-cutting concerns, deployment environments, data contracts or solution-level compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: The security concept is required because security cannot be treated as an implementation detail added after the architecture has been defined.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Where the product participates in a solution, the Product Security Concept must also align with the applicable solution trust-boundary model and enterprise security guardrails.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: The Product Security Concept should be specific to the product and its operational context.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: The concept should explain which threats are relevant, which controls are implemented, where those controls are located in the architecture, how they are verified, and who is responsible for maintaining them.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Security evidence should be connected to the relevant architecture views.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Trust boundaries and secure communication paths should be reflected in the Runtime View and Interface Specification.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Deployment-related security assumptions should be reflected in the Deployment View.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Major security trade-offs should be documented through ADRs.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Security verification results should be linked to the Verification Evidence and release readiness assessment.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Where the product participates in a solution, product-level security must be compatible with the solution security architecture.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: Missing or incomplete security evidence should be treated as product technical debt, security risk or release-readiness blocker, depending on severity.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Security Concept
proposals.statement: A product should not be considered release-ready if required security controls are only described but not implemented, verified, owned or aligned with the applicable solution and enterprise security expectations.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Verification evidence should be planned together with architecture decisions, not collected only at the end of delivery.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: A product should not wait until release readiness to discover that an architecture claim cannot be demonstrated, measured or reviewed.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: For every critical architecture decision and quality attribute, Product Architecture should define which evidence is required, how the evidence will be produced, who owns it and where it will be reviewed.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Verification evidence connects the Product Architecture Document, ADRs, quality requirements, interface specifications, security concept, deployment view and release compatibility declaration.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Evidence area | Verification intent | Required evidence

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Architecture conformance | Verify that the implemented product architecture conforms to the documented architecture decisions and required quality markers. | Architecture review record, conformance checklist, quality-marker score, ADR review, architecture deviation record

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Quality attributes | Verify that critical product quality requirements are satisfied through suitable tests or measurements. | Performance tests, resilience tests, security tests, reliability tests, scalability tests, determinism evidence

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Traceability | Verify that evidence can be traced back to the architecture decision, quality requirement, interface, security control or release criterion it supports. | Evidence traceability matrix, linked ADR, linked requirement, test reference, review record, backlog link

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Verification evidence should be defined early enough to influence backlog planning, test strategy, architecture runway and release-readiness preparation.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: If evidence depends on missing test environments, unavailable simulators, undefined interfaces, incomplete deployment automation or unclear security assumptions, the gap should be treated as product architecture runway, technical debt or release-readiness risk.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: The Product Architect is responsible for defining which architecture claims require evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Product teams are responsible for producing the implementation and test evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Security, Platform, Data and Solution Architects should be involved where the evidence affects security controls, deployment environments, data contracts, cross-product interfaces or solution baseline compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: The strength of evidence should match the criticality of the architecture claim.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Critical claims, however, require stronger evidence such as automated tests, contract tests, performance measurements, security scans, integration results, deployment records or runtime metrics.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: A product should not be considered release-ready if critical architecture claims are unsupported, outdated, unowned or not traceable to verification evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Verification Evidence
proposals.statement: Missing evidence should be recorded explicitly and handled through technical debt, release risk, architecture exception or follow-up action.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: It is required because a product can be internally complete, tested and releasable on its own, while still being incompatible with a particular solution because of interface versions, data contracts, security assumptions, deployment configuration or missing integration evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: Migration notes | Explains what is required to move from earlier versions or configurations. | Required migration steps, rollback steps, transition constraints, data migration, compatibility notes

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: Owner approval | Confirms accountable ownership for the declaration. | Product Owner approval, Product Architect approval, Product Security Owner approval if required, review date

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: The declaration should be created or updated whenever a product release is intended to participate in a solution release baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: It should also be updated when interfaces, data contracts, deployment assumptions, security controls, runtime dependencies or compatibility rules change.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: A stale compatibility declaration should not be used as release evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: The Product Architect is responsible for ensuring that the declaration is architecturally correct and supported by evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: Compatibility must always be declared against a specific baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: A product release should not simply claim to be “compatible” in general.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: It must state which solution baseline, interface versions, data model versions, security assumptions and deployment configurations it supports.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: Where compatibility cannot be fully declared, the limitation must be made explicit.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: Depending on severity, the gap should be handled as product technical debt, solution integration risk, architecture exception, release-readiness blocker or planned follow-up action.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Release Compatibility Declaration
proposals.statement: A solution release baseline should not be considered release-ready unless all participating products have current, owned and evidenced compatibility declarations.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: It is required because architecture debt is often created intentionally during delivery, but becomes dangerous when it is not documented, owned, reviewed or connected to mitigation actions.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: The register must therefore show not only what the debt is, but also why it exists, what it affects, who owns it, how it will be mitigated and whether any residual risk remains.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: The Product Risk and Technical Debt Register should be reviewed during product architecture reviews, backlog refinement, PI planning, release readiness and Inspect & Adapt.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: Open debt items that affect release compatibility, security, integration or mission-critical quality attributes must be explicitly assessed before release.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: Severity / priority | Indicates how urgently the item must be addressed. | Risk rating, priority, release relevance, affected milestone, escalation need

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: Due date | Defines when the mitigation should be completed or reviewed. | Planned resolution date, review date, release milestone, expiry date

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: A debt item without a named owner, mitigation action and review date should not be considered governed.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: The register should therefore be used as an active management tool, not as a passive list of problems.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: Product-level debt should be distinguished from solution-level debt.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: If a product debt item creates solution-level impact, it should be visible to the Solution Architect and linked to the relevant solution risk or release-readiness record.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: However, debt that affects critical security controls, release compatibility, integration evidence, safety-relevant behavior, mission-critical resilience or mandatory enterprise guardrails shall require explicit review and approval before release.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: Repeated or long-lived product debt should trigger architecture review.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Risk and Technical Debt Register
proposals.statement: In such cases, the debt should be escalated beyond the product backlog and considered in solution or enterprise architecture governance.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Level Quality Markers
proposals.statement: They should be used during product architecture reviews, backlog refinement, PI planning, implementation reviews, demos, release readiness reviews and Inspect & Adapt.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Level Quality Markers
proposals.statement: A marker should only be considered mature when it is supported by concrete evidence, such as architecture views, interface specifications, data contracts, ADRs, test results, deployment records, security evidence, observability data, compatibility declarations or technical debt records.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: They should be used during product architecture reviews, backlog refinement, PI planning, implementation reviews, product demos, release readiness reviews and Inspect & Adapt.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: A marker should only be considered mature when the required evidence is available, owned, versioned, reviewable and connected to the relevant backlog, verification, release or governance mechanism.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: ID | Marker | Review question | Required product evidence

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: P1 | Architecture completeness | Does the product architecture contain the minimum required views, decisions, quality requirements, risks and evidence? | Product Architecture Document, architecture view set, quality catalogue, ADR register, risk and debt register

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: P9 | Performance and determinism | Are latency, throughput, scheduling, resource budgets and deterministic behavior defined and measured where required? | Performance budgets, measurement results, load tests, timing analysis, resource measurements, determinism evidence

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: The product markers should be scored using the common maturity scale defined in Section 5.2.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: Product Architecture reviews should therefore distinguish between three questions.

proposals.title: SDD Product Architecture Guidelines / Product Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: Where a product marker scores low, the resulting action should be captured as product architecture runway, product technical debt, a backlog enabler, an interface clarification, a verification action, a security action, a deployment improvement, or a release-readiness follow-up.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Purpose
proposals.statement: Product reviews should be practical and decision-oriented.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Purpose
proposals.statement: They should confirm whether the product architecture is clear, whether the required evidence exists, whether ownership is assigned, whether solution compatibility is affected, and whether follow-up action is required.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Purpose
proposals.statement: A useful product review should result in one or more of the following outcomes: approval, conditional approval, required rework, architecture enabler, technical debt item, exception request, release-readiness blocker or solution-level escalation.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Purpose
proposals.statement: Accepted with actions | Architecture is acceptable but improvement actions are required

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Purpose
proposals.statement: Conditionally accepted | A risk or gap must be resolved before a defined milestone

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Purpose
proposals.statement: Escalated | Decision requires higher-level architecture or portfolio involvement

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Product reviews shall be staged across the lifecycle.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Release readiness requires stronger evidence, especially for critical interfaces, data contracts, security controls, deployment reproducibility, resilience, performance, observability and compatibility with solution baselines.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of interoperability should be supported by interface contracts and integration evidence.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of security should be supported by threat models, security reviews or verification evidence.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of deployability should be supported by deployment manifests, pipeline evidence or environment validation.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of release compatibility should be supported by a Product Release Compatibility Declaration and solution baseline mapping.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Product reviews must also check whether product-level architecture changes affect solution compatibility.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: A product-level ADR may require solution-level review if it changes an externally visible interface, data model, security assumption, runtime dependency, deployment assumption, compatibility declaration or release baseline.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: The following principles should guide product architecture reviews:

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Evidence over presentation | Claims must be proven through documents, tests, demos, measurements, or operational evidence

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Lightweight but mandatory | Reviews should be efficient, but critical architecture markers cannot be skipped

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Cross-level alignment | Enterprise, Solution, and Product implications must be visible

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Early review | Critical architecture issues should be reviewed before implementation becomes expensive

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Review Principles
proposals.statement: Continuous feedback | System demos, Inspect & Adapt, and operational findings must update architecture

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: It focuses on the architecture of one product, including context, building blocks, runtime behavior, deployment, interfaces, data contracts, ADRs, quality requirements, security, verification evidence, release compatibility and technical debt.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: Security, Data and Platform Architects should be involved where the review affects security controls, data contracts, deployment environments, DevSecOps, observability or runtime assumptions.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect should be involved whenever product architecture changes affect solution interfaces, data flows, deployment topology, security boundaries, solution baselines or release compatibility.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: The review should apply the Product Architecture quality markers together with the mandatory BAPO alignment markers.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: The business contribution must be clear, the product architecture response must be defined, the required delivery and verification mechanisms must exist, and ownership must be assigned.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: A product architecture should not be considered architecture-ready if these dimensions are unclear.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: Review findings must not remain informal observations.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: They should be assigned to owners and tracked through backlog items, debt registers, release-readiness records or architecture review actions.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Release Readiness
proposals.statement: The Product Architect provides the product architecture evidence required for the review.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Release Readiness
proposals.statement: A product release shall not be considered ready if critical architecture evidence is missing, if externally visible interfaces or data contracts are not verified, if security or deployment evidence is incomplete, or if compatibility with the applicable solution baseline and enterprise guardrails is not declared and evidenced.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Demo, Evidence and Technical Debt Feedback
proposals.statement: The Product Architect shall ensure that architecture-relevant findings are converted into owned follow-up actions.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Demo, Evidence and Technical Debt Feedback
proposals.statement: If a finding affects a solution baseline, interface version, data contract, security boundary, deployment topology or release compatibility, it shall be escalated to Solution Architecture.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Demo, Evidence and Technical Debt Feedback
proposals.statement: If repeated findings indicate unclear enterprise guardrails, missing platform capability or recurring product-line debt, the feedback should also be made visible to Enterprise Architecture.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Product-level exceptions are required when a product cannot fully comply with an applicable enterprise guardrail, solution baseline, interface contract, data contract, security expectation, runtime assumption, deployment constraint, quality marker or release compatibility requirement.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: The Product Architect is responsible for identifying the exception and providing the required rationale, impact assessment, mitigation proposal and evidence.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: If the deviation affects a solution baseline, interface version, data model, security boundary, deployment topology or release compatibility, the Solution Architect shall be involved.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Approved product exceptions shall be linked to the Product Architecture Document, ADR Register, Product Risk and Technical Debt Register, Product Release Compatibility Declaration or release-readiness record.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Exceptions that affect solution compatibility shall also be visible to Solution Architecture.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Product exceptions should remain visible until they are closed, expired or renewed.

proposals.title: Product Architecture Review and Feedback / Product Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Repeated product exceptions should be reviewed as architecture feedback and may indicate missing architecture runway, unclear guardrails, insufficient platform support or unresolved solution-level constraints.
